title: Kth Smallest Product of Two Sorted Arrays
summary: Given two sorted integer arrays nums1 and nums2, and an integer k, find the k-th (1-based) smallest product of elements nums1[i] * nums2[j] where 0 <= i < nums1.length and 0 <= j < nums2.length.
statement: Given two sorted integer arrays nums1 and nums2, and an integer k, find the k-th (1-based) smallest product of elements nums1[i] * nums2[j] where 0 <= i < nums1.length and 0 <= j < nums2.length.
constraints: nums1 and nums2 are sorted integer arrays with lengths up to 50000 and values within ±100000.
Consider all len(nums1)*len(nums2) pair products with multiplicity.
Return the one-based kth smallest product.
hints: Binary-search a product value and count how many pairs are at most it.
For each first value, use upper bound for positive, all-or-none for zero, and a ceiling threshold with lower bound for negative.
If count(mid)>=k move high to mid, else low to mid+1.
The count is monotone in the product limit and handles inequality reversal exactly, so lower-bound search returns the smallest value with at least k products—precisely the kth product.
editorial: The count is monotone in the product limit and handles inequality reversal exactly, so lower-bound search returns the smallest value with at least k products—precisely the kth product.

tests.explanation: The products are six, eight, fifteen, and twenty; the second is eight.
Sorted products are -16,-8,-8,-4,0,0,6,12; the sixth is zero.
